analysis.scope_and_question: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic RNA viruses with a worldwide distribution and the capacity to cause severe human disease. More than 40 hantavirus species have been identified, of which over 20 are known to be pathogenic to humans. Old World hantaviruses are classically associated with Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), whereas New World hantaviruses predominantly cause Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS), a condition characterized by rapid progression to respiratory failure, shock, and substantial mortality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review summarizes current knowledge on hantavirus biology, reservoirs, transmission, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, laboratory diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, and prevention, with particular emphasis on the situation in Spain.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human infection is usually acquired through the inhalation of aerosols contaminated with excreta from infected reservoir animals, primarily rodents, although person-to-person transmission has been demonstrated for the Andes virus. Diagnosis relies mainly on serological and molecular methods. No universally effective antiviral therapy is currently available for hantavirus disease, and management remains largely supportive, with intensive care and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation playing a crucial role in severe cases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Worldwide, hantavirus infections remain underdiagnosed because many cases are asymptomatic or present with nonspecific clinical manifestations. Evidence accumulated over the last three decades confirms the circulation of hantaviruses in Spain, both in animal reservoirs and in humans. Although clinically recognized disease remains uncommon, serological and ecological studies demonstrate that these infections are present in the country.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Continued surveillance, improved diagnostic awareness, and the development of effective preventive and therapeutic strategies remain important public health priorities.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides a global overview of hantavirus infections, focusing on their biology, transmission, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, with particular emphasis on the situation in Spain. Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic RNA viruses causing severe diseases like HFRS and HCPS. Human infection typically occurs through inhalation of aerosols from infected rodents, though person-to-person transmission has been observed with Andes virus. Diagnosis relies on serological and molecular methods, but no universally effective antiviral therapy exists, with management being largely supportive. Despite underdiagnosis due to asymptomatic or nonspecific cases, evidence confirms hantavirus circulation in Spain. Continued surveillance, improved diagnostic awareness, and development of preventive and therapeutic strategies are critical public health priorities.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak, examining its transmission dynamics, clinical presentation, and implications for maritime travel medicine. The central question concerns the characteristics and management of this rare travel-associated zantavirus event.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the ANDV outbreak, including its biology, transmission, clinical features, diagnostics, and management. The review does not specify databases, search dates, or study counts, as it is a narrative synthesis rather than a systematic review.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: As of July 2026, 13 cases (12 confirmed, 1 probable) were reported, with 3 deaths. Transmission was likely land-based before embarkation, with limited onboard human-to-human spread, and was contained after a 42-day follow-up period. Severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome progresses rapidly, requiring intensive supportive care.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights preparedness gaps in shipboard triage, contact tracing, specimen transport, genomic surveillance, risk communication, and cross-border follow-up. No licensed antiviral therapy or vaccine is available, and the outbreak underscores challenges in early recognition and management.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening One Health-informed pre-travel counseling, post-travel symptom surveillance, and maritime outbreak protocols is essential. Improved coordination for zoonotic threats in expedition travel is needed, along with enhanced diagnostic and management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus outbreak, a rare travel-associated zoonotic event with 13 cases (12 confirmed, 1 probable) and 3 deaths. Transmission likely occurred before embarkation, with limited onboard spread, and was contained after 42 days. Severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome progresses rapidly, requiring intensive supportive care due to the lack of licensed antivirals or vaccines. The outbreak reveals critical gaps in shipboard preparedness, including triage, contact tracing, and genomic surveillance. Future priorities include strengthening One Health-informed pre-travel counseling, post-travel surveillance, and maritime outbreak protocols to address zoonotic threats in expedition travel.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hantavirus epidemiology, ecology, and clinical recognition, diagnostics, and preparedness in Europe, with emphasis on endemic Puumala virus (PUUV), Dobrava virus (DOBV), and Seoul virus (SEOV), and clarifies the relevance of imported Andes virus (ANDV) infection for travel medicine and maritime response.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A structured narrative review of literature published from January 2000 to May 2026, prioritising surveillance reports, systematic and narrative reviews, rodent ecology studies, diagnostic evaluations, external quality assessment studies, and outbreak investigations. WHO, ECDC, and International Health Regulations guidance documents were also reviewed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: European hantavirus epidemiology is heterogeneous and shaped by reservoir ecology, biome-specific rodent dynamics, clinical awareness, diagnostic capacity, and surveillance practice. Climate effects are indirect and regionally variable, mediated by mast years, predator-prey dynamics, winter conditions, land use, reservoir density, and human exposure.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Diagnostic preparedness is uneven, particularly for molecular detection. Imported ANDV infection is rare in Europe but relevant to travel medicine and high-consequence preparedness because it can cause severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and, unlike endemic European hantaviruses, has documented person-to-person transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: European preparedness should prioritise PUUV, DOBV, and SEOV through rodent biomonitoring, harmonised surveillance, improved molecular diagnostics, and locally calibrated early warning. The 2026 MV Hondius cruise-ship cluster of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) infections has highlighted urgent gaps in European preparedness for both endemic and imported hantavirus disease.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines hantavirus risk and preparedness in Europe, focusing on endemic viruses (PUUV, DOBV, SEOV) and imported ANDV. It highlights heterogeneous epidemiology shaped by rodent ecology, climate effects, and diagnostic disparities. Key gaps include uneven molecular diagnostic capacity and the need for improved preparedness for imported ANDV, which can cause severe disease and person-to-person transmission. Recommendations include rodent biomonitoring, harmonised surveillance, and early warning systems tailored to local conditions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the origin and evolutionary history of the Andes virus responsible for a multi-country outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome among passengers and crew of a cruise ship in 2026.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed complete ANDV small (S), medium (M), and large (L) genome segment sequences from Chile alongside outbreak-associated and publicly available genome sequences to trace the geographic origin of the outbreak-associated virus.
analysis.methods: Complete ANDV genome segment sequences from Chile were analyzed alongside outbreak-associated and publicly available sequences, and phylogeographic analysis was performed to determine the genetic relationship and geographic origin of the outbreak virus.
analysis.main_results: The outbreak virus clustered within an ANDV Clade III cluster spanning southern Chile and northern Patagonia in Argentina and was most closely related to a human-derived ANDV collected in Los Rios Region of Chile in 2012; phylogeographic analysis showed that the genetically distinct ANDV Clade V lineage circulating in central Chile was not closely related to the cruise ship outbreak-associated genomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings trace the geographic origin of the outbreak-associated virus to a defined corridor, the Hua Hum Pass, a cross-border zone connecting Neuquen Province in Argentina with the Los Rios and La Araucania Regions of Chile, representing a novel identification of the outbreak's origin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide critical information for surveillance and prevention efforts by identifying the specific geographic region where the outbreak virus originated, which can help in targeting public health interventions to prevent future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is high as it is based on complete genome sequence analysis and phylogeographic analysis, but limitations include the potential for incomplete sampling of viral strains in the region and the reliance on publicly available sequences which may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the origin and evolutionary history of the Andes virus responsible for a 2026 cruise ship outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. By analyzing complete ANDV genome sequences from Chile alongside outbreak-associated sequences, researchers found the outbreak virus clustered within ANDV Clade III, closely related to a 2012 human-derived strain from Chile's Los Rios Region. Phylogeographic analysis traced the outbreak's origin to the Hua Hum Pass, a cross-border zone between Argentina and Chile. This identification of the specific geographic corridor provides critical insights for surveillance and prevention efforts, though the study's strength is tempered by potential sampling limitations and reliance on publicly available sequences.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a Perspective article that analyzes the outbreak through a narrative synthesis of available evidence, without reporting specific study designs, populations, or meta-analytic methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the hantavirus outbreak highlighted critical gaps in pandemic preparedness, particularly in international coordination and response mechanisms, and emphasizes the need for systemic reforms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a lack of standardized protocols for cross-jurisdictional coordination and limited data on the effectiveness of current response strategies, which remain unresolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests the need for improved surveillance systems, enhanced communication frameworks, and updated guidelines for managing outbreaks of hantaviruses and similar pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, emphasizing its role in exposing vulnerabilities in global health preparedness. It outlines the need for reforms in operational authority and cross-jurisdictional coordination. The review is a narrative synthesis of available evidence, highlighting gaps in standardized protocols and data on response effectiveness. It proposes specific research and practice implications, including improved surveillance and updated guidelines for managing hantavirus outbreaks and similar pathogens.

analysis.scope_and_question: Hantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses responsible for two severe human diseases: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review summarizes genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and AI-enabled approaches in hantavirus research.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Although single-layer genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics studies have advanced our understanding of hantavirus biology, true multi-omics integration remains scarce, leaving systems-level mechanisms of disease severity and host–pathogen interactions unresolved.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Proteomics has revealed host proteins involved in immune regulation, endothelial dysfunction, and potential therapeutic targeting, whereas metabolomics indicates substantial metabolic reprogramming during infection, although dedicated studies remain limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: AI-based approaches are increasingly applied to outbreak prediction, surveillance, and risk modeling. Drawing on successful multi-omics frameworks developed for other viral infections, we discuss opportunities to improve biomarker discovery, surveillance, therapeutic development, and future precision medicine strategies for hantavirus infections.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the application of omics technologies in hantavirus research, focusing on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches. Hantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses causing severe human diseases such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). While single-layer omics studies have enhanced understanding of viral biology, multi-omics integration is still limited, leaving unresolved systems-level mechanisms of disease severity and host–pathogen interactions. Proteomics has identified host proteins involved in immune regulation and endothelial dysfunction, but metabolomics studies are still limited. AI-based methods are increasingly used for outbreak prediction and risk modeling, and the review highlights opportunities for improving biomarker discovery, surveillance, and therapeutic development for hantavirus infections.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus infection causes life-threatening hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) due to severe endothelial barrier breakdown, with clinical severity varying widely and no targeted endothelial-protective treatments available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study synthesized four core lines of evidence from metagenomic reports, re-analysis of three public GEO datasets (GSE245916, GSE7271, GSE270172), and experimental findings on FXR/TGR5 agonists and HTNV effects.
analysis.methods: Researchers re-analyzed public GEO datasets via standardized RNA-seq/microarray pipelines, examined endothelial cell receptor expression, tested FXR/TGR5 agonists in inflammation and vascular injury models, and investigated HTNV's impact on cholesterol metabolism and bile acid precursors.
analysis.main_results: SEOV-infected human/rat lung endothelial cells showed conserved VCAM1/ICAM1 upregulation; SEOV-infected rat lung displayed sustained Nfkb1 suppression and Slc10a2 downregulation; PUUV 3D vessel chips featured IL6 elevation and disrupted BA transporters; TGR5 was undetectable in endothelial cells; FXR/TGR5 agonists repressed NF-κB inflammation and mitigated lung vascular injury; HTNV upregulated CH25H to block HMGCR-dependent cholesterol synthesis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors propose a unified pathogenic model where hantavirus-triggered gut dysbiosis and impaired cholesterol metabolism deplete circulating FXR/TGR5 agonistic bile acids, relieving inhibition of endothelial NF-κB and monocyte NLRP3 inflammasomes to exacerbate capillary leakage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The gut microbiota–bile acid–FXR/TGR5 axis represents a repurposable therapeutic target for hantavirus diseases, offering a testable roadmap for clinical multi-omics cohorts, in vitro receptor modulation assays, and in vivo pharmacological interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Direct causal evidence connecting bile acid signaling to viral vascular damage remains absent, though the evidence strength is high due to the integration of multiple datasets and experimental findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates hantavirus-induced endothelial barrier dysfunction by examining the role of bile acid signaling. The authors synthesized evidence from metagenomic reports, re-analysis of public datasets, and experimental work, showing that hantaviruses disrupt gut microbiota and cholesterol metabolism, leading to depletion of FXR/TGR5 agonistic bile acids. This loss removes constitutive inhibition of NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasomes, exacerbating capillary leakage. The study identifies the gut microbiota–bile acid–FXR/TGR5 axis as a novel therapeutic target, though direct causal evidence is still needed. The findings provide a framework for future validation through clinical, in vitro, and in vivo studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate hantavirus exposure among wildlife farmers in Vietnam, addressing a knowledge gap about zoonotic disease risks in this high-risk occupation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 210 wildlife farmers in Lao Cai and Dong Nai provinces, Vietnam, between August 2023 and March 2024.
analysis.methods: Researchers tested farmers for hantavirus antibodies to determine prior exposure and current infection status, focusing on those exclusively involved in wildlife farming without hunting or processing activities.
analysis.main_results: 8.7% of wildlife farmers tested positive for hantavirus antibodies, indicating prior exposure, while 1.9% had suspected recent infections during the study period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that wildlife farming itself poses a significant hantavirus risk independent of direct animal handling, highlighting an underrecognized transmission pathway.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Results emphasize the need for enhanced surveillance and biosecurity measures in wildlife farms across Southeast Asia to prevent zoonotic hantavirus transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the large sample size and targeted population provide moderate evidence for occupational risk assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated hantavirus exposure among 210 wildlife farmers in Vietnam, finding 8.7% had antibodies indicating prior infection and 1.9% had suspected recent infections. The research reveals that wildlife farming itself poses significant hantavirus risk independent of direct animal handling, suggesting an underrecognized transmission pathway. These findings highlight the need for enhanced surveillance and biosecurity measures in wildlife farms across Southeast Asia to prevent zoonotic disease spread.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap of limited systematic comparisons of virome compositions across urbanization gradients by investigating urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted large-scale sampling in two densely populated Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, with distinct climates, collecting 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans.
analysis.methods: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents, enabling identification of vertebrate-associated viruses and assessment of their zoonotic potential.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43), and discovered two viruses previously unreported in rodents.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as revealing cross-order transmission risk and highlighted the importance of spatial distance in shaping the distribution and transmission of rodent-borne viruses, with meteorological variables independently explaining 5.0% of the variation in viral community composition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights are essential for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments, particularly for viruses with zoonotic potential like Orthohantavirus seoulense.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it provides comprehensive virome data but may have limitations in generalizability beyond the sampled cities and rodent species.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities using metagenomic sequencing. Sampling 1,072 rodents from four species in Wuhan and Shenzhen, the researchers identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and HCoV_OC43). They also discovered two previously unreported rodent viruses, revealing cross-order transmission risks. The analysis showed that meteorological variables explained 5.0% of viral community composition divergence between cities. These findings highlight the importance of spatial distance in virus distribution and provide critical insights for proactive surveillance and mitigation of zoonotic threats in urban environments.

analysis.event: Review published in JAMA Neurology examines neurologic complications of hantavirus infection following a cruise ship outbreak of Andes virus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 11 cases reported, 3 deaths; HPS mortality rate 35-50%; neurologic complications include headaches, blurred vision, vomiting, meningitis, encephalitis, pituitary damage, and rare peripheral neuropathy or stroke.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: No FDA-approved antivirals or vaccines available; some drugs in pre-clinical trials; need for prospective studies with long-term follow-up; underreporting likely due to rural settings; calls for improved communication to prevent stigma while emphasizing isolation importance.

analysis.brief_en: A recent JAMA Neurology review highlights neurologic complications of hantavirus infection following a cruise ship outbreak that infected 11 people and killed three. Hantaviruses, rodent-borne viruses, can cause hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) or hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), each with distinct neurologic risks. HPS, prevalent in the Americas, often leads to secondary neurologic issues like headaches and seizures, while HFRS, endemic in Asia and Eastern Russia, more commonly involves direct neurologic complications such as blurred vision and pituitary damage. Despite severe manifestations, no FDA-approved treatments exist, and research is limited by underreporting in rural settings. Experts call for prospective studies and improved public communication to address stigma and misinformation while emphasizing isolation to control spread.

analysis.scope_and_question: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic pathogens responsible for two major clinical syndromes: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome/cardiopulmonary syndrome.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review comprehensively synthesizes current evidence on hantavirus virology, taxonomy, reservoir ecology, transmission dynamics, global epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and One Health surveillance strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Particular emphasis is placed on the immunopathological mechanisms underlying endothelial dysfunction and vascular hyperpermeability, the hallmark features of severe disease.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Key research gaps identified include inadequate surveillance in South Asia and Africa, insufficient understanding of Andes virus human-to-human transmission, limited validation of rapid diagnostics, and unresolved mechanisms of immune-mediated pathology.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Adopting a One Health perspective, this review proposes priority research and public health directions to strengthen global preparedness, improve outbreak prediction, and accelerate development of effective diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines against hantavirus disease.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of hantavirus disease, covering global epidemiology, immunopathogenesis, clinical management, and future research priorities. It highlights the immunopathological mechanisms underlying severe disease, including endothelial dysfunction and vascular hyperpermeability. The review critically evaluates current diagnostic approaches and emphasizes therapeutic limitations, particularly the lack of universally effective antivirals and approved vaccines. Key research gaps include inadequate surveillance in South Asia and Africa, limited understanding of Andes virus human-to-human transmission, and unresolved immune-mediated pathology mechanisms. The study proposes a One Health approach to strengthen global preparedness, improve outbreak prediction, and accelerate the development of effective diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study investigated the evolutionary history and consequences of reassortment in Tula orthohantavirus (TULV) in a hybrid zone between evolutionary lineages of its reservoir host, the common vole, to understand how host hybridization enables the emergence of reassorted hantavirus lineages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted across 58 trapping sites with 127 infected voles, focusing on a 12.5 km broad hybrid zone where parental TULV clades contact each other.
analysis.methods: Phylogenomic analyses were performed to detect reassortment events, and in silico 3D modeling of seven glycoproteins was used to analyze structural variations in the N-terminal region of the glycoprotein.
analysis.main_results: Three independent reassortment events were detected, with most of the host hybrid zone dominated by a single strain with a reassorted M-Segment encoding the surface glycoprotein; clade-specific variation in the glycoprotein's N-terminal region, including five residues with two showing evidence of positive selection, was observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that reassortment between parental TULV clades in the contact region resulted in a transgressive virus phenotype potentially adapted to hybrid hosts, demonstrating the potential of zones of hybridization for the emergence of new virus strains with novel evolutionary trajectories.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This research highlights the role of host hybridization in driving viral evolution and the emergence of new hantavirus strains, which could inform surveillance strategies in areas with hybrid host populations and improve understanding of hantavirus emergence dynamics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Leptospirosis and hantavirus disease are important zoonoses with rodents as main reservoirs. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and genetic diversity of Leptospira and hantavirus in rodents from rural Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus is a rodent-borne zoonotic disease in which rodents serve as the primary reservoir, while humans acquire infection through spillover exposure. The model incorporated Brownian stochastic perturbations, discrete time delays, and exponential delay-survival effects to capture incubation, survival, and environmental uncertainty.
analysis.methods: An SIR–SIR transmission framework was formulated for rodent and human populations, extended with Brownian stochastic perturbations, discrete time delays, and exponential delay-survival effects. Qualitative properties, disease-free and endemic equilibria, reproduction numbers, and extinction/persistence conditions were established using stochastic threshold analysis.
analysis.main_results: Hantavirus persistence is primarily governed by rodent-to-rodent transmission, while human infections arise through spillover from infected rodents. Stochastic perturbations and delay-survival effects reduce the effective reproduction threshold under certain conditions and can promote disease extinction. Numerical simulations showed consistent solutions across methods, with SNSFD exhibiting superior stability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The proposed stochastic delay model provides a mathematically rigorous and biologically realistic framework for studying hantavirus transmission. The results highlight that controlling infection within the rodent reservoir is the most effective strategy for reducing disease persistence and limiting human spillover.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the importance of reservoir-driven transmission dynamics and suggest that targeting rodent populations is critical for hantavirus control. The improved stability of the SNSFD method makes it suitable for simulating stochastic epidemic systems with delays, aiding in public health risk assessments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a mathematical modeling analysis without empirical validation, limiting its direct applicability to real-world scenarios. However, the rigorous theoretical framework and consistent numerical results provide moderate confidence in the model's biological plausibility and utility for understanding transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a stochastic delay differential model to assess hantavirus spillover risk in Europe, focusing on rodent-to-human transmission dynamics. Using an SIR–SIR framework with stochastic perturbations and time delays, the model demonstrated that rodent-to-rodent transmission governs persistence, while human infections result from spillover. Stochastic effects and delays can reduce transmission under certain conditions. The SNSFD numerical method showed superior stability for simulations. The findings underscore that controlling rodent reservoirs is the most effective strategy for limiting human spillover, providing a mathematically rigorous tool for public health risk assessment.

2f9c71279007d904258d95e6399ed0495c12b7be.text: 汉坦病毒 感染:全球概况和西班牙现状

488881c0cdb94f7b1f4261ef49798704938a4c46.text: 汉坦病毒 是啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患 RNA 病毒,在全球范围内分布,能够引起严重的人类疾病。已鉴定出 40 多种汉坦病毒物种,其中 20 多种已知对人类致病。旧世界汉坦病毒通常与 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 相关,而新世界汉坦病毒主要引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS),这种疾病的特征是快速进展为呼吸衰竭、休克和严重的 死亡率。人类感染通常是通过吸入受感染的 储存宿主 动物(主要是啮齿类动物)排泄物污染的气溶胶而获得的,尽管安第斯山脉病毒已被证明存在人与人之间的 传播 感染。本综述总结了目前关于汉坦病毒生物学、储存宿主、传播、流行病学、临床表现、实验室 诊断、治疗、预后和预防的知识,特别强调了西班牙的情况。在世界范围内,汉坦病毒 感染仍未得到充分诊断,因为许多病例无症状或出现非特异性临床表现。诊断主要依靠血清学和分子学方法。目前还没有普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法可用于汉坦病毒疾病,治疗仍以支持性为主,重症监护和体外膜肺氧合在严重病例中发挥着至关重要的作用。过去三十年积累的证据证实了汉坦病毒在西班牙的传播,无论是在动物 储存宿主 中还是在人类中。尽管临床上认可的疾病仍然不常见,但血清学和生态研究表明这些感染在该国存在。继续 监测、提高诊断意识以及制定有效的预防和治疗策略仍然是重要的公共卫生优先事项。

f4c148309c94326d298edc4f94e810288505e8ab.text: 巡航相关的安第斯病毒和严重的汉坦病毒肺病:叙述性回顾

51b5dcbe3427f890781464f42b6ca052b5cedb61.text: 2026 年与邮轮相关的安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 暴发 代表了一种罕见但后果严重的旅行相关人畜共患病事件,结合了登船前可能的陆上感染、船上有限的人际传播 传播、延迟的临床识别以及多国公共卫生协调。这篇叙述性综述综合了 暴发、ANDV 生物学、传播 动力学、临床表现、诊断、管理以及对海上和探险旅行医学的影响的当前证据。截至 2026 年 7 月 2 日,世界卫生组织 (WHO) 报告了与 Hondius 暴发 机动船 (M/V) 有关的 13 例病例,其中包括 12 例实验室确诊感染、1 例疑似病例和 3 例死亡。在对所有已确定的接触者完成 42 天的随访期且没有出现其他继发病例后,世卫组织认为 传播 已中断,暴发 已得到遏制。现有证据支持可能在登船前发生陆地传播,随后在船上进行有限的人际传播 传播,但没有持续传播。严重的汉坦病毒心肺综合征可能始于非特异性发热、不适、肌痛、胃肠道症状或呼吸系统不适,然后突然进展为肺水肿、休克和致命的心肺衰竭。由于没有获得许可的 抗病毒药物 疗法或 疫苗 可用,因此早期识别、谨慎的液体管理、重症支持护理、通气支持以及及时转移到重症监护或具有体外膜氧合能力的中心仍然是核心。暴发 强调了船上分类、接触者追踪、标本运输、基因组监测、风险沟通和跨境后续方面的关键准备差距。加强 One Health 旅行前咨询、旅行后症状 监测 和海上 暴发 协议对于未来与探险相关的人畜共患威胁至关重要。

54ebeae021d4d000f7fcb2204df89c76e5023129.text: 该综述重点关注 2026 年与邮轮相关的安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 暴发,检查其 传播 动态、临床表现以及对海上旅行医学的影响。核心问题涉及这一罕见的与旅行相关的赞塔病毒事件的特征和管理。

ca74091c98a84a29e383513ea46a26e9736e8937.text: 这篇叙述性综述综合了 ANDV 暴发 的当前证据,包括其生物学、传播、临床特征、诊断和管理。该综述没有具体说明数据库、检索日期或研究计数,因为它是叙述性综合而不是系统综述。

e136850cb97eb26aedcc20bbe69f5d32fcb2d2ec.text: 汉坦病毒 气候变化和全球流动时代欧洲的风险和准备。

43281af9e7e27dfc5c49627c75b72730160872f9.text: 背景:汉坦病毒 是啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患病,导致肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。在欧洲,普马拉病毒和多布拉瓦病毒是最常见的疾病;首尔病毒与港口和城市环境有关。2026 年 MV Hondius 游轮出现安第斯山脉汉坦病毒(ANDV) 感染群,涉及来自 23 个国家的乘客,这突显了欧洲在预防地方性和输入性汉坦病毒疾病方面的紧迫差距。目的:回顾欧洲的汉坦病毒流行病学、生态学和临床识别、诊断和准备,重点关注地方性普马拉病毒 (PUUV)、多布拉瓦病毒 (DOBV) 和首尔病毒 (SEOV),并阐明输入性安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 感染与旅行医学和海上应对的单独相关性。资料来源:我们对 2000 年 1 月至 2026 年 5 月发表的文献进行了结构化叙述性综述,优先考虑 监测 报告、系统和叙述性综述、啮齿动物生态学研究、诊断评估、外部质量评估研究和 暴发 调查。还审查了 WHO、ECDC 和《国际卫生条例》指导文件。内容:欧洲汉坦病毒流行病学 是异质的,由 储存宿主 生态、生物群落特异性啮齿动物动力学、临床意识、诊断能力和 监测 实践塑造。气候影响是间接的且因地区而异,由肥大年份、捕食者-猎物动态、冬季条件、土地利用、储存宿主 密度和人类暴露介导。诊断准备情况参差不齐,尤其是分子检测方面。输入性 ANDV 感染在欧洲很少见,但与旅行医学和高后果准备有关,因为它可导致严重的汉坦病毒心肺综合征,并且与欧洲流行的汉坦病毒不同,已记录了人与人之间的 传播。影响:欧洲的准备工作应通过啮齿动物生物监测、协调的 监测、改进的分子诊断和本地校准的预警来优先考虑 PUUV、DOBV 和 SEOV。

a884e67610a91b076f7cb80874a1580de283ae30.text: 安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 于 2026 年在一艘游轮的乘客和船员中引起了多国 暴发 和 暴发。为了调查导致 暴发 的病毒的起源和进化历史,我们分析了来自智利的完整 ANDV 小 (S)、中 (M) 和大 (L) 基因组 片段序列以及与 暴发 相关且公开的序列基因组 序列。在所有三个特定区段的系统发育中,暴发 病毒聚集在横跨智利南部和阿根廷巴塔哥尼亚北部的 ANDV 进化枝 III 簇中,并且与 2012 年在智利洛斯里奥斯地区收集的人源 ANDV (p1236) 关系最密切,代表了 暴发 相关病毒已知的最接近的历史亲戚。系统发育地理学分析表明,在智利中部流行的遗传上不同的ANDV Clade V谱系与暴发相关游轮基因组没有密切关系,从而降低了指示病例在经过马乌莱地区时通过人畜共患跨物种溢出获得感染的可能性。这些发现将 暴发 相关病毒的地理起源追溯到一个明确的走廊,即华胡姆山口,这是一个连接阿根廷内乌肯省与智利洛斯里奥斯和拉阿劳卡尼亚地区的跨境区域。

ebc96ec0095ba36dac47ab52d295d7367f23b0ce.text: 该研究旨在调查导致2026年一艘游轮乘客和船员中发生多国暴发 汉坦病毒肺综合征的安第斯病毒的起源和进化历史。

babd4b95c489896ad1fb151f0480993d99f0dbee.text: 该研究分析了来自智利的完整 ANDV 小 (S)、中 (M) 和大 (L) 基因组 片段序列以及 暴发 相关和公开的 基因组 序列,以追踪 暴发 相关病毒的地理起源。

d30967766045200b292ef2d413f0a8c30599f746.text: 对来自智利的完整 ANDV 基因组 片段序列与 暴发 相关序列和公开序列进行了分析,并进行了系统发育分析,以确定 暴发 病毒的遗传关系和地理起源。

aac57432ca5adbc56adcf506fa1606f890eae513.text: 暴发 病毒聚集在横跨智利南部和阿根廷巴塔哥尼亚北部的 ANDV Clade III 簇内,与 2012 年在智利洛斯里奥斯地区收集的人源 ANDV 最密切相关;系统发育地理学分析表明,在智利中部流行的遗传上独特的ANDV Clade V谱系与暴发游轮相关的基因组没有密切关系。

4355283a8c45c307921c4f0349dab95c1b8f6756.text: 这些发现将 暴发 相关病毒的地理起源追溯到一个明确的走廊——Hua Hum Pass,这是一个连接阿根廷内乌肯省与智利洛斯里奥斯和拉阿劳卡尼亚地区的跨境区域,代表了对 暴发 起源的新鉴定。

2be2edb9e6666f6289e46a406322643aa172ead7.text: 这些发现通过确定 暴发 病毒起源的特定地理区域,为 暴发 和预防工作提供了关键信息,这有助于制定公共卫生干预措施,以预防未来的 暴发。

efeb7bfa732ce039e2141943d285da645156c672.text: 该研究的证据强度很高,因为它基于完整的 基因组 序列分析和系统发育地理学分析,但其局限性包括对该地区病毒株的采样可能不完整,以及对公开序列的依赖可能会引入偏差。

1e7bd326fd37e1996c2251d4c0324e0c7dd0dba6.text: MV Hondius汉坦病毒暴发——流行病防范的经验教训

91a3fca4696d9511cc86f5f0f9cff513687b5e7d.text: 本视角探讨了 MV Hondius 上的汉坦病毒暴发,研究它如何揭示全球卫生准备中的漏洞,并概述旨在提高跨司法管辖区的操作权限和协调的改革。

a8e84ff705671df4f7c3b3ba0de0f86cffc2e410.text: 此次审查的重点是 MV Hondius 上的汉坦病毒暴发,审查其如何暴露全球卫生准备方面的弱点,并提出改革建议,以加强跨司法管辖区的操作权限和协调。

75dc90e78346551ae4a5d12ed66de001979fee10.text: 该评论是一篇观点文章,通过对现有证据的叙述性综合来分析 暴发,但没有报告具体的研究设计、人群或荟萃分析方法。

23712ac290819fb1ffd1c73c6289ed1c093c1cf1.text: 审查的结论是,汉坦病毒 暴发 强调了大流行病防范方面的关键差距,特别是在国际协调和应对机制方面,并强调了系统性改革的必要性。

7f60c7d4a20ec58a667ae46bbb20b8142926376a.text: 审查发现,缺乏跨司法管辖区协调的标准化协议,并且有关当前应对策略有效性的数据有限,这些问题仍未得到解决。

92e0b069790b392b43db3f4d648eaa184e701154.text: 该审查建议需要改进 监测 系统、增强通信框架以及更新管理 暴发 和类似病原体的指南。

d36a218f56917478ce49a167f6419e5ef0f4b1f6.text: 汉坦病毒 研究中的组学方法:当前进展、挑战和未来展望

65d67ecc1346b92e81026c9df1f64cca05806bb5.text: 汉坦病毒 是人畜共患 RNA 病毒,可导致两种严重的人类疾病:肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。全球病死率从 1% 到 40% 不等。尽管单层基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学和代谢组学研究增进了我们对汉坦病毒生物学的理解,但真正的多组学整合仍然很少,导致疾病严重程度和 宿主 与病原体相互作用的系统级机制尚未解决。高通量组学技术极大地推进了 汉坦病毒–宿主 相互作用的研究。这篇综述总结了汉坦病毒研究中的基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学和人工智能支持的方法。基因组研究阐明了病毒多样性、进化 和重配,而转录组学则确定了控制内皮细胞和先天 免疫应答 的调控网络。蛋白质组学揭示了 宿主 蛋白参与免疫调节、内皮功能障碍和潜在的治疗靶向,而代谢组学表明感染期间存在大量的代谢重编程,尽管专门的研究仍然有限。基于人工智能的方法越来越多地应用于 暴发 预测、监测 和风险建模。借鉴为其他病毒感染开发的成功的多组学框架,我们讨论了改进生物标志物发现、监测、治疗开发以及汉坦病毒感染的未来精准医学策略的机会。

d2b50680615b0c9516cde476d5eaddfaa03809cb.text: 汉坦病毒 是人畜共患 RNA 病毒,可导致两种严重的人类疾病:肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。

e9bf8cca342af21752489033174f0846349a2870.text: 这篇综述总结了汉坦病毒研究中的基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学和人工智能支持的方法。

99cabb32cfe0bd48adaac50aac61cdf83fd6c301.text: 尽管单层基因组学、转录组学、蛋白质组学和代谢组学研究增进了我们对汉坦病毒生物学的理解,但真正的多组学整合仍然很少,导致疾病严重程度和 宿主 与病原体相互作用的系统级机制尚未解决。

afbc4950aa109c69a821f3a7bc2970726a79507c.text: 蛋白质组学揭示了 宿主 蛋白参与免疫调节、内皮功能障碍和潜在的治疗靶向,而代谢组学表明感染期间存在大量的代谢重编程,尽管专门的研究仍然有限。

196e56775b128b87f05b5754c12efafc0691c4f1.text: 基于人工智能的方法越来越多地应用于 暴发 预测、监测 和风险建模。借鉴为其他病毒感染开发的成功的多组学框架,我们讨论了改进生物标志物发现、监测、治疗开发以及汉坦病毒感染的未来精准医学策略的机会。

0504f3ce6ccd4287b41786555b2e3a0ae85cb37a.text: 肠道-血管界面的胆汁酸信号传导:汉坦病毒 内皮屏障功能障碍的新型调节剂

99bca8166ee6c5819996786788d8ffd6d65475db.text: 汉坦病毒 感染会引发危及生命的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS),其原因是严重的内皮屏障破坏和全身毛细血管渗漏。临床严重程度因未定义的 宿主 调节剂而异,并且不存在靶向内皮保护 治疗。最近的数据将汉坦病毒与肠道微生物组重塑联系起来,而胆汁酸 (BA) 受体 FXR 和 TGR5 有效抑制 NF-κB 介导的内皮炎症。我们综合了四个核​​心证据。首先,宏基因组报告证实汉坦病毒重塑了啮齿动物 储存宿主 的肠道/肺部微生物群。其次,我们通过标准化 RNA-seq/微阵列流程重新分析了三个公共 GEO 数据集:(i)GSE245916:SEOV 感染的人/大鼠肺 EC 显示保守的 VCAM1/ICAM1 上调(人 VCAM1 log 2 FC=+1.17,P = 0.023;大鼠 Icam1 log 2 FC=+0.32,padj=0.016) FXR 未改变;(ii) GSE7271:SEOV 感染的大鼠肺表现出持续的 Nfkb1 抑制(所有时间点,P<0.05)和第 15 天 Slc10a2 下调(P = 0.028);(iii) GSE270172:PUUV 3D 血管芯片具有稳健的 IL6 升高(log 2 FC=+1.22,P = 3.1×10 -8 )和破坏的 BA 转运蛋白(ABCC3 log 2 FC=−1.44,P = 7.4×10 - 12)。所有数据集中的内皮细胞中均检测不到 TGR5 (GPBAR1)。第三,FXR/TGR5激动剂抑制NF-κB炎症并减轻肺血管损伤。第四,HTNV 上调 CH25H 以阻断 HMGCR 依赖性胆固醇合成,消耗 BA 前体底物。我们提出了一个统一的致病模型:汉坦病毒 触发的肠道菌群失调加上病毒受损的胆固醇代谢消耗循环 FXR/TGR5 激动性 BA,解除内皮 NF-κB 和单核细胞 NLRP3 炎性体的组成性抑制,从而加剧毛细血管渗漏。我们定义了分层的可测试预测,涵盖临床多组学 队列研究、体外受体调节测定和体内药理学干预。尽管仍缺乏将 BA 信号转导与病毒血管损伤联系起来的直接因果证据,但肠道微生物群 -BA-FXR/TGR5 轴代表了汉坦病毒疾病的可重新利用的治疗靶点;我们的框架为后续验证提供了严格的可测试路线图。

3fe1aa59f9983268da7ae55c76831613c30c9a49.text: 汉坦病毒 感染会因严重的内皮屏障破坏而导致危及生命的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS),临床严重程度差异很大,并且没有针对性的内皮保护 治疗 可用。

f0c20454623e9fb4f05c549a3c604f04d63f274d.text: 该研究综合了来自宏基因组报告的四个核心证据、对三个公共 GEO 数据集(GSE245916、GSE7271、GSE270172)的重新分析以及 FXR/TGR5 激动剂和 HTNV 效应的实验结果。

91d4ea413b351a0fda1de307b2e151d4968ef1ca.text: 研究人员通过标准化 RNA-seq/微阵列流程重新分析了公共 GEO 数据集,检查了内皮细胞受体表达,在炎症和血管损伤模型中测试了 FXR/TGR5 激动剂,并研究了 HTNV 对胆固醇代谢和胆汁酸前体的影响。

9a8149c9518a1b53caded34f25548dc14d3a4505.text: 感染 SEOV 的人/大鼠肺内皮细胞表现出保守的 VCAM1/ICAM1 上调;SEOV 感染的大鼠肺表现出持续的 Nfkb1 抑制和 Slc10a2 下调;PUUV 3D 血管芯片具有 IL6 升高和 BA 转运蛋白中断的特征;在内皮细胞中检测不到 TGR5;FXR/TGR5 激动剂抑制 NF-κB 炎症并减轻肺血管损伤;HTNV 上调 CH25H 以阻断 HMGCR 依赖性胆固醇合成。

d086b2d6bbafcf945aa6c160e7643c5e69e938ab.text: 作者提出了一个统一的致病模型,其中汉坦病毒触发的肠道菌群失调和胆固醇代谢受损会消耗循环中的 FXR/TGR5 激动性胆汁酸,从而缓解内皮 NF-κB 和单核细胞 NLRP3 炎症小体的抑制,从而加剧毛细血管渗漏。

c5a1cbfe57ed5b26f4f2b1620142b959961c11cc.text: 肠道微生物群-胆汁酸-FXR/TGR5 轴代表了汉坦病毒疾病的可重复利用的治疗靶点,为临床多组学 队列研究、体外受体调节测定和体内药理干预提供了可测试的路线图。

3456ba6bcd4a87e95ffe89051cf11efe415e206c.text: 尽管由于多个数据集和实验结果的整合,证据强度很高,但将胆汁酸信号传导与病毒血管损伤联系起来的直接因果证据仍然不存在。

5d4e09e2a7f71ce93fb212d6fd5b92a56cbd05ef.text: 该研究旨在调查越南野生动物养殖者中汉坦病毒的暴露情况,解决这一高风险职业中人畜共患疾病风险的知识差距。

99776b65aeb4880e186e609ecfcd10f2fd6ee3f5.text: 2023 年 8 月至 2024 年 3 月期间,对越南老街省和同奈省的 210 名野生动物农民进行了一项横断面研究。

8c0a081eb0e6d8afb8985b5ed59d42400d38e5b3.text: 研究人员对农民进行了汉坦病毒抗体测试,以确定之前的暴露情况和当前的感染状况,重点关注那些专门从事野生动物养殖而不进行狩猎或加工活动的农民。

fbd251e7a556d32cb1b6cf9e10ee482270f39504.text: 8.7% 的野生动物养殖者汉坦病毒抗体检测呈阳性,表明之前接触过,而 1.9% 的野生动物养殖者在研究期间怀疑最近感染过。

1b1f237165124c50ff8ff5790722a2296b4cc986.text: 研究结果表明,野生动物养殖本身会带来重大的汉坦病毒风险,与直接动物处理无关,凸显了一条未被充分认识的 传播 途径。

bb9dcf4b6f017d1f77b5c997e401a0b848b6de55.text: 结果强调需要在东南亚野生动物农场加强 监测 和生物安全措施,以防止人畜共患汉坦病毒传播。

9e70f440e01d7f95010715c49afea90b72ab3584.text: 该研究的横断面设计限制了因果推断,但大样本量和目标人群为职业风险评估提供了适度的证据。

0f5eac640859b53f65e17cefaf80febd0664293e.text: 汉坦病毒 在越南野生动物养殖场被发现:东南亚的警报

a3884206df38fbbc11ade11c381b26083e771915.text: 宏转录组学揭示了中国特大城市中城市化驱动的啮齿动物病毒组和人畜共患病风险的差异。

84105d2667be01db8e19842de7ea9d86c75ea83a.text: 宏基因组测序增进了我们对野生动物相关病毒的理解,并能够识别潜在的人畜共患病原体。然而,大多数研究仍然局限于地理范围,很少对不同城市化梯度的病毒组组成进行系统比较。为了解决这一差距,我们在两个人口稠密、气候不同的大城市——武汉和深圳进行了大规模采样。我们收集了来自四个经常与人类互动的物种的 1,072 只啮齿动物,从而能够对啮齿动物的城市直肠病毒动态和人畜共患病风险进行比较分析。我们鉴定出 35 种与脊椎动物相关的病毒。其中,9个潜在新种,包括诺如病毒和正双核病毒属,3个具有人畜共患潜力,即汉城正汉坦病毒和人类冠状病毒OC43(HCoV_OC43)。我们还在啮齿类动物中发现了两种以前未报告的病毒,即刺猬首尔正汉坦病毒和犬星状病毒,这揭示了跨目 传播 风险。此外,还发现了 22 种高风险病毒,其中武汉和深圳表现出明显的 患病率 模式。我们的分析表明,城市间直肠病毒组差异是由气象变量构成的,独立解释了病毒群落组成变异的 5.0%。我们的研究结果强调了空间距离在影响啮齿动物传播病毒的分布和 传播 方面的重要性。这些见解对于主动采取 监测 和缓解高密度城市环境中新出现的人畜共患威胁至关重要。

62ecab807c3431da1eaf376a2bb345020232ae15.text: 该研究旨在通过调查中国特大城市中城市化驱动的啮齿动物病毒组差异和人畜共患风险,来解决不同城市化梯度下病毒组组成的有限系统比较的知识差距。

cb13b2e062f9a153daeb39457282599df342abbe.text: 该研究在中国两个人口稠密、气候独特的大城市武汉和深圳进行了大规模采样,从四个经常与人类互动的物种中收集了 1,072 只啮齿动物。

9a704d432c40e9c617be6216b36e9b974b2aa823.text: 宏基因组测序用于分析啮齿动物的直肠病毒组动态和人畜共患风险,从而能够识别脊椎动物相关病毒并评估其人畜共患潜力。

3114be5b5bc2013b6a865f617d63869c66f6af18.text: 该研究鉴定了 35 种与脊椎动物相关的病毒,包括 9 种潜在的新物种和 3 种具有人畜共患潜力的病毒(首尔正汉坦病毒和人类冠状病毒 OC43),并发现了两种此前在啮齿类动物中未报告的病毒。

a8cd4fdb0bfc52121f4815c31b515ff793077005.text: 作者将这些发现解释为揭示了跨序 传播 风险,并强调了空间距离在影响啮齿动物传播病毒的分布和 传播 方面的重要性,其中气象变量独立解释了病毒群落组成变异的 5.0%。

a05fdc21db15b5d80bff3e5a9882f550637ec6aa.text: 这些见解对于主动采取 监测 和缓解高密度城市环境中新出现的人畜共患威胁至关重要,特别是对于像首尔正汉坦病毒这样具有人畜共患潜力的病毒。

3f417eb6a09fbffb63280d55d595295897288025.text: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它提供了全面的病毒组数据,但在抽样城市和啮齿动物物种之外的普遍性上可能存在局限性。

960b42545fe255c09c5a83d8bc3b6488132a786c.text: 欧盟协调对汉坦病毒暴发 的响应 - DD News

7bc7ea8225874f5612db859ab79bdb335d77fc40.text: 发布日期:2026 年 7 月 22 日。活动日期:2026 年 5 月 6 日(欧盟民事保护机制激活),持续响应持续至 2026 年 7 月 12 日。

9276034e45cddee68da726972990d2dfe1d496b9.text: 欧洲,特别是特内里费岛(西班牙)。受影响人群:MV Hondius 游轮上的乘客和船员。

39147ba86454dcf88ca7b13ae4108ab1e509335e.text: JAMA Neurology 最近的一篇评论强调了汉坦病毒感染的神经系统并发症,此前一艘游轮 暴发 导致 11 人感染并导致 3 人死亡。汉坦病毒是啮齿动物传播的病毒,可引起 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS) 或 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS),每种病毒都有不同的神经系统风险。HPS 在美洲流行,通常会导致继发性神经系统问题,如头痛和癫痫发作,而 HFRS 在亚洲和俄罗斯东部流行,更常见的是直接神经系统并发症,如视力模糊和垂体损伤。尽管症状严重,但尚不存在 FDA 批准的 治疗,并且农村地区的研究因报告不足而受到限制。专家呼吁进行前瞻性研究并改善公众沟通,以解决耻辱和错误信息,同时强调隔离以控制传播。

60ca831ea85254d7c0ec0cfffe6ff79799bd265d.text: 汉坦病毒 疾病:全球 流行病学、免疫发病机制、临床管理和未来研究重点的综述

f565501ecb1603ac46e4a789887400f82ed16ff5.text: 汉坦病毒 是啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患病原体,可导致两种主要临床综合征:肾综合征出血热 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征/心肺综合征。尽管近几十年来汉坦病毒研究取得了重大进展,但 监测、诊断、治疗和 疫苗 开发仍面临重大挑战。本综述全面综合了汉坦病毒病毒学、分类学、储存宿主 生态学、传播 动力学、全球 流行病学、发病机制、临床表现、诊断、治疗、预防和 One Health 监测 策略的当前证据。特别强调内皮功能障碍和血管通透性过高的免疫病理学机制,这是严重疾病的标志特征。该评论进一步探讨了气候变化、土地利用变化、生物多样性丧失和啮齿动物种群动态如何影响 跨物种溢出 风险和地理扩张。当前的诊断方法,包括 血清学、RT-PCR 和下一代测序,与新兴的护理点技术一起接受严格评估。强调了治疗局限性,特别是缺乏普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 和全球批准的 疫苗。已确定的关键研究差距包括南亚和非洲的 监测 不足、对安第斯山脉病毒人传人 传播 的了解不足、快速诊断的验证有限以及免疫介导的病理学机制尚未解决。本综述采用“One Health”的视角,提出了优先研究和公共卫生方向,以加强全球准备,改进 暴发 预测,并加速开发针对汉坦病毒疾病的有效诊断、治疗方法和 疫苗。

c27c4a285df7a85afbc84848c59e17ecf561abec.text: 宿主 杂交使重配汉坦病毒谱系的出现

4dbbecaca43f03a28e85338db3ca1bf935fc4d60.text: 个体之间遗传物质的交换是 进化 和大多数生命分支多样化的关键驱动力。分段病毒可以通过基因组片段的重配来交换遗传物质。重配产生的新病毒株可以具有更大的感染范围和更高的毒力,尽管重配病毒在自然界中除流感之外的适应性优势的具体例子仍然很少。我们在这里研究了图拉正汉坦病毒(TULV)在其 储存宿主 宿主(普通田鼠)进化谱系之间的混合区中重配的后果。在 58 个诱捕点和 127 只受感染的田鼠中,我们在亲代 TULV 进化枝接触处的 12.5 公里宽的区域中检测到了 27 个 TULV 重配体,类​​似于与 宿主’ 一致的病毒杂交区域。系统基因组分析揭示了三个独立的重配事件,但大多数 宿主 杂交区由具有重配 M 片段的单一菌株主导,该片段编码表面糖蛋白。我们检测到糖蛋白 N 末端区域由五个残基组成的进化枝特异性变异,其中两个残基显示出正选择的证据。七种糖蛋白的计算机 3D 建模证实,该 N 末端区域对于每个 TULV 进化枝和主要重配体都具有独特且特定的结构,并且是 TULV 糖蛋白唯一的结构可变区域。我们的研究结果表明,接触区亲本 TULV 进化枝之间的重配导致了可能适应杂种 宿主 的越界病毒表型。这证明了杂交区对于出现具有新颖进化轨迹的新病毒株的潜力。

62efa19cd3e8aa471f6e04d4194af65902535166.text: 该研究调查了图拉正汉坦病毒(TULV)在其 储存宿主 宿主(普通田鼠)进化谱系之间的杂交区中重配的后果,以了解 宿主 杂交如何导致重配汉坦病毒谱系的出现。

35f9fdbf55addfdc9fe593c29ea70264586560df.text: 该研究在 58 个诱捕点进行,涉及 127 只受感染的田鼠,重点关注 12.5 公里宽的混合区,其中亲本 TULV 进化枝相互接触。

59d804689086660f807fbb1601a55df1ab891940.text: 进行系统基因组分析以检测重配事件,并使用七种糖蛋白的计算机 3D 建模来分析糖蛋白 N 末端区域的结构变异。

93d2c620c45618ed634521bd170920c47f858e06.text: 检测到三个独立的重配事件,大部分 宿主 杂交区由具有编码表面糖蛋白的重配 M 片段的单一菌株主导;观察到糖蛋白 N 末端区域的进化枝特异性变异,包括五个残基,其中两个显示出正选择的证据。

f793f7000f1152b3cd85a13defa5000e23561f53.text: 研究结果表明,接触区亲本 TULV 进化枝之间的重配导致了一种可能适应杂交 宿主 的侵入病毒表型,这证明了杂交区域对于出现具有新进化轨迹的新病毒株的潜力。

8bc5f09a22b789589bdcc8c7e66ab9e6eb5df4e8.text: 这项研究强调了宿主杂交在驱动病毒进化和新汉坦病毒毒株的出现中的作用,这可以为宿主杂交种群地区的监测策略提供信息,并提高对汉坦病毒出现动态的理解。

dc09f0f5235fa43b42a14a5ca0f3fd8918656027.text: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它依赖于系统基因组学和计算机分析,而没有对海侵表型进行实验验证;局限性包括该研究的观察性质以及混合区中可能存在未考虑的混杂因素。

11655e643c9457a534e7b4a153004695705dbc24.text: 气候变化是南亚汉坦病毒风险的放大器:一个被忽视的联系

803489bb6ac9fa797c60ff58bf3bffe43f85367c.text: 摘要汉坦病毒在南亚人群和啮齿动物 储存宿主 中得到血清流行病学证实,在印度的职业风险人群中证实了抗汉坦病毒抗体,在斯里兰卡证实了与慢性肾病的独立关联,并且在超过五分之一的住院钩端螺旋体病患者中发现了与钩端螺旋体病的合并感染。尽管如此,这些发现与该地区日益加剧的季风洪水、快速城市化和气候驱动的啮齿动物生态的交叉点仍然完全未经检验。这封信强调了被忽视的气候与 传播 之间的关系,指出了放大南亚 传播 风险的结构性脆弱性,并呼吁在整个地区进行综合洪水应对 传播 和 One Health 协调。

b8820a1c2183ad32c670d14ef83d52b0d14a8986.text: 本研究解决了检查季风洪水和城市化等气候变化因素与南亚汉坦病毒风险的交叉点的需要,其中汉坦病毒在人群和啮齿动物 储存宿主 中建立了血清流行病学。作者强调了对这种被忽视的联系缺乏关注。

a7ed29577f1ee9c35f0bd7dd52d9687ab0094c22.text: 该研究是一封信,概述了南亚目前对汉坦病毒的了解,重点关注其在人类和啮齿动物 储存宿主 中的存在,特别是在印度和斯里兰卡。它还注意到住院患者中存在钩端螺旋体病合并感染情况。

35f8f0d161adbc0497e529ca7b4458fbed98dcd2.text: 所提供的证据中没有明确详细说明方法部分,但该研究依赖于印度现有的血清流行病学数据和职业风险群体的观察,以及与斯里兰卡慢性肾病和钩端螺旋体病合并感染模式的独立关联。

bd123f3d3740cceabaf64103ff56af2f80c4208e.text: 在印度的职业风险群体中证实了抗汉坦病毒抗体,在斯里兰卡证实了与慢性肾脏病的独立关联,并且在超过五分之一的住院钩端螺旋体病患者中发现了与钩端螺旋体病的合并感染。

7a4082fa354f4d9baafc521147c40e9c2eb33e6c.text: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了被忽视的气候-传播 关系,并确定了放大南亚 传播 风险的结构性脆弱性。这是对综合洪水响应 监测 和 One Health 协调的新颖呼吁。

448982ba39b536ce050df98bfb61ecccccc4a5e7.text: 研究结果可为综合洪水响应 监测 系统的开发提供信息,并强调“同一个健康”协调对于应对气候变化和城市化背景下汉坦病毒带来的风险的重要性。

c1c42757ce633dff23ca8c906c2a5b33b6e35670.text: 该研究基于现有的血清流行病学数据,不包括新的实验或临床发现,这限制了证据的强度。然而,这些观察结果是基于特定地区和人群报告的数据。

79ec180b992e55d4f1444fc6bb6b0eae4b582869.text: 安第斯病毒诱导趋化因子主导的内皮和基质激活模式,促进免疫细胞的招募。

b51e67a05f49577a105d95aa62bf17c1256c75d8.text: 传统上,安第斯病毒感染是通过过度促炎 宿主 反应导致肺毛细血管渗漏和心肺衰竭的框架来解释的。1-5 然而,我们之前的内皮细胞发现 6 与当前的成纤维细胞数据一起,表明汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS) 背后有一种更微妙的免疫致病机制,其特征不是经典的广义细胞因子风暴,而是选择性的、细胞特异性的趋化因子驱动的炎症特征。

c8591748d9d1982c1788044f5d8e58e60ed4206b.text: 免疫细胞在汉坦诱导的 肾综合征出血热 中的作用

70a722b0b164538c3efcd88fed774c813a523973.text: 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 是一种严重且常常致命的人畜共患疾病,主要由正汉坦病毒属成员汉坦病毒 (HTNV) 引起。尽管已知免疫细胞在 HTNV 诱导的 HFRS 中发挥关键作用,但在疾病过程中不同免疫亚群的详细动态变化、表型改变和功能特征仍然知之甚少。在这篇综述中,我们总结了目前对 HTNV 感染过程中关键免疫群体的认识,包括单核细胞、巨噬细胞、树突状细胞 (DC)、自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞、中性粒细胞、T 细胞和 B 细胞。我们强调了中心免疫学的二元性,其中这些细胞对于病毒清除是必需的,同时也参与免疫病理组织损伤。通过整合临床和机制见解,我们提出了一个详细的框架,用于理解保护性免疫和免疫病理学之间的平衡如何决定疾病结果。认识这些复杂的动态对于指导未来的研究和确定 HFRS 的潜在治疗靶点至关重要。

1e2ef1ae059113d28aaacdfa1b5f49246d83839c.text: 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 是一种严重且常常致命的人畜共患疾病,主要由正汉坦病毒属成员汉坦病毒 (HTNV) 引起。该综述重点关注免疫细胞在 HTNV 诱导的 HFRS 中的作用,旨在了解不同免疫亚群在疾病过程中的详细动态变化、表型改变和功能特征。

f0739a9853de0db40444cb5c1cfd501bb03ab868.text: 本综述总结了目前对 HTNV 感染过程中关键免疫群体的认识,包括单核细胞、巨噬细胞、树突状细胞 (DC)、自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞、中性粒细胞、T 细胞和 B 细胞。该综述整合了临床和机制见解,提出了一个框架,用于理解 HFRS 中保护性免疫和免疫病理学之间的平衡。

bea5f450724351bd9fde0a4166ac84b47b9f1824.text: 该综述强调了免疫学的中心二元性,即免疫细胞对于病毒清除是必需的,同时也参与免疫病理组织损伤。保护性免疫和免疫病理学之间的平衡决定了 HTNV 诱导的 HFRS 的疾病结果。

e412af3fd5932e8257cc86734b3c4ed2e080c8e8.text: 在 HTNV 诱导的 HFRS 过程中,不同免疫亚群的详细动态变化、表型改变和功能概况仍然知之甚少。需要进一步研究来阐明 HFRS 中 免疫应答 的复杂动力学。

a8f65c6969142610bfbe0eda749651533b00b0b0.text: 认识到 HFRS 中 免疫应答 的复杂动态对于指导未来的研究和确定潜在的治疗靶点至关重要。需要进一步研究来了解 HTNV 诱导的 HFRS 中保护性免疫和免疫病理学之间的平衡。

8b3e190d66df9871176ce37c7b5ce899654bd349.text: 汉坦病毒:人畜共患病病原体及其在实现可持续发展中的作用

9631b40a7ba35b6754004a75354a6799419c4890.text: 人畜共患病,即动物与人类之间感染的 传播,仍然是全世界人类和兽医卫生机构面临的挑战。尽管各个医学领域取得了进步,但在根除人畜共患病原体和预防其复发(尤其是病毒病原体)方面仍然失败。这些人畜共患病毒中的一种是汉坦病毒(单链RNA),该病毒的出现因其高死亡率率而引起恐慌和恐惧。该感染主要通过小鼠等啮齿动物传播给人类,导致 肾综合征出血热 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征 等严重疾病。因此,回顾这种感染的基本信息、环境因素的作用和 传播 的模式对于预防至关重要,能够避免感染并减轻人类、动物和经济损失。感染控制最重要的策略之一是实施“同一个健康”方法,该方法将人类、动物和环境健康(金三角)紧密结合起来,并与实现可持续发展目标 (SDG) 相关。该方法旨在全面改善环境、兽医护理和人类福祉。

3c6be539dddf66a0ca48ac9bee6985deaddc3cca.text: 2023-2025年兰溪市啮齿动物中患病率和人畜共患钩端螺旋体和汉坦病毒的遗传多样性

4ef4b78b25807721f0b3ae6258893f8c62b84b8c.text: 钩端螺旋体病和汉坦病毒病是重要的人畜共患病,其中啮齿类动物是主要的储存宿主病。本研究旨在调查浙江省兰溪市农村啮齿动物中钩端螺旋体和汉坦病毒的患病率和遗传多样性。

f73f9cfd15049b1b1591298e62f36d2910bccbf8.text: 该研究于2023年4月至2025年8月在浙江省兰溪市农村进行。共捕获啮齿类动物350只,其中褐家鼠为优势种(80.00%)。

e1715928a847b43d69e2670497345ac334becc9f.text: 通过肝脏和肾脏组织的无菌解剖收集样品。采用实时荧光PCR检测病原核酸,对阳性样本进行基因测序和系统发育分析。

2ce5480cd87882e5c3eaae48cd07aedd137db32c.text: 钩端螺旋体总体携带率为7.14%(25/350),汉坦病毒携带率为1.43%(5/350)。未检测到两种病原体的双重感染。所有汉坦病毒分离株均为首尔病毒 (SEOV),与 疫苗 株表现出高度遗传差异。

efa7255b276c540020173e72ad4101edf6c83131.text: 作者解读,兰溪农村啮齿类动物钩端螺旋体携带率较高,其中汉坦病毒以SEOV为主。A unique local phylogenetic cluster of Leptospira borgpetersenii was identified,indicating potential 疫苗 mismatch and local evolutionary divergence.

0432ea0975d23d6642a15d508f907bc97fac119e.text: 由于携带率高、遗传变异大,应加强有针对性的监测和防控措施。自然遗传变异表明潜在的抗原漂移和 疫苗 匹配减少,需要进一步的血清学验证。

ce96d6aef25d83bdbc78df93f728b796220b2786.text: 该研究是在特定地理区域进行的,限制了普遍性。由于样本量大且缺乏合并感染数据,证据强度中等。

5bde929166aaed924459f95a3d611a6d83a73110.text: 背景:钩端螺旋体病(由钩端螺旋体属细菌引起)和汉坦病毒病(由汉坦病毒病毒引起)是重要的人兽共患病,以啮齿动物为主要储存宿主。本研究调查了浙江省兰溪市农村地区啮齿动物中钩端螺旋体和汉坦病毒的患病率和遗传多样性。啮齿动物的钩端螺旋体携带率高于全国平均水平。所有汉坦病毒分离株均为汉城病毒(SEOV),与疫苗菌株显示出高度遗传分化。值得注意的是,鉴定出一个独特的钩端螺旋体波氏螺菌(Leptospira borgpetersenii)本地系统发育簇,表明潜在的疫苗不匹配和局部进化分化。方法:样本采集时间为2023年4月至2025年8月,2023-2024年每年4月至8月进行密集捕获,2025年4月进行额外采样。通过无菌解剖收集肝脏和肾脏组织。使用实时荧光PCR检测病原体核酸,并对阳性样本进行基因测序和系统发育分析。结果:共捕获350只啮齿动物,以褐家鼠(Rattus norvegicus)为优势物种(80.00%)。总体钩端螺旋体携带率为7.14%(25/350),在R. norvegicus中携带率最高。总体汉坦病毒携带率为1.43%(5/350),主要分布在褐家鼠和黄胸鼠(Rattus flavipectus)中。未检测到两种病原体共感染。遗传分析鉴定出12株钩端螺旋体为问号钩端螺旋体(Leptospira interrogans),2株为波氏钩端螺旋体(L. borgpetersenii);后者与国内外菌株存在遗传差异,提示潜在的进化趋势。两株汉坦病毒均为汉城病毒,与2021年国内汉城病毒株密切相关,但与疫苗菌株(如80-39、Z37)的核苷酸同源性仅为86.08-86.81%,表明自然变异。结论:兰溪市农村啮齿动物的钩端螺旋体携带率相对较高,汉坦病毒以汉城病毒型为主。褐家鼠是两种病原体的主要宿主。应加强针对性监测和预防控制措施。自然遗传变异提示潜在的抗原漂移和疫苗匹配度降低,需要进一步血清学验证。应关注病原体遗传变异对防控工作的影响。

b9ad585bd2b073b435196e639be0bc6db0c784f4.text: 使用随机延迟模型对欧洲啮齿动物驱动的汉坦病毒跨物种溢出 进行公共卫生风险评估

f7913d2a089b9d17985055c37f950308eb0eccd0.text: 简介汉坦病毒是一种啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患疾病,其中啮齿类动物是主要的 储存宿主,而人类则通过 跨物种溢出 接触而感染。为了更好地了解环境变异和延迟疾病动态对 传播 的影响,本研究开发了一种随机延迟微分模型,该模型结合了汉坦病毒传播的生物学相关特征。方法 为啮齿动物和人类群体的相互作用制定了 SIR-SIR 传播 框架。通过结合布朗随机扰动、离散时间延迟和指数延迟生存效应来扩展确定性模型,以捕获孵化、生存和环境不确定性。建立了模型的定性属性,包括正性、有界性、可行性和适定性。得出无病和地方性平衡,并获得确定性和随机繁殖数。使用随机阈值分析研究消光和持久性条件。使用 Euler-Maruyama、随机 Runge-Kutta 和随机非标准有限差分 (SNSFD) 方法进行数值模拟。结果分析表明,汉坦病毒 的持久性主要受啮齿类动物之间的 传播 控制,而人类感染则通过受感染的啮齿类动物的 跨物种溢出 产生。随机扰动和延迟生存效应在某些条件下降低了有效繁殖阈值,并可以促进疾病灭绝。理论研究结果得到了数值模拟的支持,数值模拟表明所有三种数值方法都能为小时间步长提供一致的解决方案。然而,SNSFD 方案保留了正性,并在较大的时间步长和较强的随机扰动下表现出优异的数值稳定性。纳入了 2026 年报告的汉坦病毒更新,以激励模型并强调 储存宿主 驱动的 传播 动态的持续重要性。讨论所提出的随机延迟模型为研究汉坦病毒传播 提供了数学上严格且生物学上现实的框架。结果强调,控制啮齿动物 储存宿主 内的感染是减少疾病持续性和限制人类 跨物种溢出 的最有效策略。SNSFD 方法稳定性的提高也使其成为模拟具有延迟的随机流行病系统的合适计算方法。

35c8b7aba8cb5eb95e163305f996c8e5fa5fa1c8.text: 汉坦病毒是一种啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患疾病,其中啮齿类动物是主要的储存宿主,而人类则通过接触跨物种溢出而受到感染。本研究旨在开发随机延迟微分模型,以了解环境变异性和延迟疾病动态对汉坦病毒传播 的影响。

b38ba3bec38b8bd0ef42cc09e9b56b1ddaa33adb.text: 该研究使用 SIR-SIR 传播 框架开发了一个随机延迟微分模型,用于啮齿动物和人类群体的相互作用。该模型结合了布朗随机扰动、离散时间延迟和指数延迟生存效应,以捕获孵化、生存和环境不确定性。

b0c0dcd1a3a8393e470ad797ad9527d08142f308.text: 针对啮齿动物和人类群体制定了 SIR-SIR 传播 框架,并通过布朗随机扰动、离散时间延迟和指数延迟生存效应进行了扩展。使用随机阈值分析建立定性特性、无病和地方性平衡、繁殖数和灭绝/持续条件。

46d550b963920d41fcc4c35a5aff04792754952a.text: 汉坦病毒 的持久性主要由啮齿类动物之间的 传播 控制,而人类感染则通过受感染的啮齿类动物的 跨物种溢出 产生。随机扰动和延迟生存效应在某些条件下降低了有效繁殖阈值,并可以促进疾病灭绝。数值模拟显示了各种方法的一致解决方案,并且 SNSFD 表现出卓越的稳定性。

add6e094cca476b5f5b931e3f7597a55d6c8e361.text: 所提出的随机延迟模型为研究汉坦病毒传播 提供了数学上严格且生物学上现实的框架。结果强调,控制啮齿动物 储存宿主 内的感染是减少疾病持续性和限制人类 跨物种溢出 的最有效策略。

0d3f828f206007d28e99a26074c44197f14dcfcc.text: 研究结果强调了 储存宿主 驱动的 传播 动力学的重要性,并表明针对啮齿动物种群对于汉坦病毒控制至关重要。SNSFD 方法稳定性的提高使其适合模拟具有延迟的随机流行病系统,有助于公共卫生风险评估。

7e28762177c78dad23190928c2048a8f27a173b0.text: 该研究是一种未经实证验证的数学模型分析,限制了其对现实场景的直接适用性。然而,严格的理论框架和一致的数值结果为模型的生物学合理性和理解 传播 动力学的实用性提供了一定的信心。

b27a33ed9a3daa22365c762316631bdcb043f776.text: 汉坦病毒 Merupakan 病毒 人兽共患病 anggota 属 Orthohantavirus yang menjadi penyebab penyakit infeksi 新兴登甘廷卡特病和死亡 yang tinggi。病毒可通过尿液、唾液、啮齿类动物唾液传播。秘鲁的 iklim、城市化、秘鲁的 penggunaan lahan、serta meningkatnya interaksi antara manusia 和 储存宿主 berkontribusi terhadap meningkatnya risiko transmisi汉坦病毒di berbagai wilayah、termasuk Indonesia。汉坦病毒旧世界汉坦病毒和新世界汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS)。Manifestasi klinis bervariasi dari demam akut Hingga gagal ginjal atau gagal napas dengan angka fatalitas yang dapat mencapai 30–50% pada HCPS。诊断 包括详细的病史、临床表现、血清学分析和 RT-PCR 分子分析。您可以使用特定的防病毒软件来保护您的隐私,并提供支持。印度尼西亚,infeksi汉坦病毒diperkirakan masih mengalami underdiagnosis dan underrereporting,meskipun bukti serologis dan molecularkuler menunjukkan adanya Sirkulasivirus pada manusia maupun rodensia.汉坦病毒 merupakan penyakit 人兽共患病 新兴阳 berpotensi menjadi ancaman凯塞哈坦马西亚拉卡特。印度尼西亚 Klinis 诊所、Penguatan 监测器、Deteksi Dini、Pengendalian Rodensia、Serta Penerapan Pendekatan One Health 策略

fc94f164e70663c2a4273c9fc46d903dbdfb362b.text: 汉坦病毒 是正汉坦病毒属中的一种人畜共患病毒,可引起新发传染病,发病率和 死亡率 发病率很高。

e19465af1a702d61150801bcda2970fbf7e7633d.text: 诊断是通过结合病史、临床表现、血清学检查和RT-PCR分子检测而建立的。

e7cb6c74140af9e97d9b35ca69aa5ef595420450.text: 汉坦病毒 是一种啮齿动物传播的病原体,由于其高 死亡率 发病率和严重疾病的可能性,对公共卫生构成重大威胁。该病毒通过接触受感染的啮齿动物或其排泄物传播,引起不同的综合症:美洲为 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS),欧洲和亚洲为 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS)。早期症状与普通流感相似,通常导致 诊断 和 治疗 延迟。该病毒的危险在于它能够触发过多的免疫应答,导致血管渗漏和器官衰竭。虽然人与人之间的 传播 很少见,但清洁棚屋或农业工作等活动可能会使人暴露于空气中的病毒颗粒。目前的 治疗 是支持性的,强调氧疗和器官监测。尽管与其他呼吸道疾病相比,该病毒的 发病率 相对较低,但公共卫生专业人员仍然对该病毒的严重性感到担忧。
